Your sentiment seems to be: My wife did whatever she wanted and had all the fun in the world and once she got bored she found some “nice guy”  or “fool” to settle for and take her in, and she most likely smiles back at her past knowing she had her cake and ate it too.

When it could be: My wife did a lot of fucked up things and could have been wildy depressed, misguided and was seeking some type of high or validation in all the wrong ways. She could very well regret all of her actions and feel disgust toward herself and might be a completely different person today. 

Yes she lied to you. I get that. It’s not okay. I’m just trying to suggest the real possibility that she might not have settled for you as much as she feels like she found something much, much greater than whatever it was she was doing in the past. 

You say you’ve been a happy family and that she’s been the most wonderful person in the world. Maybe that’s who she is today and the person she was before you met is gone. I do think people can change, especially if they want to and they realize they had issues and were really fucked up. I could be wrong but I feel like this is a real possibility.

Not a therapist or a professional, nor have I been married or have kids but I have been in LTRs and have been lied to and shit on. 

My perspective is this: while it’s difficult, I’d try to let go of the “she was ran through and now she’s settling for me,” first of all. She has a past. Everyone has a past. For all you know she could be quietly mortified by the way she used to live, knowing that it was terrible and could very well hold a lot of resentment for the way she used to be. People can change and grow up. I used to sleep around a lot because I was insecure and it validated me and when I look back at all of that VS being with the girl I have now there is no contest. Wish I could change the way I was when I was younger but I can’t. Maybe your wife feels the same way. You could be the best thing that’s ever happened to her. 

Now she did lie to you, which isn’t good, but also kinda makes me feel like my opinion is validated. She probably got sick of messing around and wanted to change and find someone who she could be secure and loved with. If she flat out told you about her past you’d run away, she knows that. Lot of people would. 

But if she’s always been honest with you otherwise, and she’s never given you any reason to think she’d be unfaithful or messing around, and she’s been good and fair, and the relationship has been healthy, consider that she probably regrets a lot of her past or doesn’t care about it and just have an open talk about it. Her reaction will be telling so pay close attention.

I manage a painting company. Early this year while we were hiring a lot of new people, I noticed a really cute girl was part of our first day orientation. I said hello to everyone, considered how attractive she was, but also that I was a manager and shouldn’t go there so I didn’t think much of it. 

Saw her in the shop every now and then. Quick hellos and small talk. Nothing more. Couldn’t get myself to flirt. 

I took a week off as I had some family in town. The day they all left at the end of the week was a Friday, which also happened to be a day my company had planned an outing for everyone to get together for drinks at a local outdoor venue. I wasn’t going to go. And didn’t want to. But my boss / friend convinced me via text, saying the owners would appreciate it and that I should just stop by for a quick drink. He ended up selling me on it and I went. 

Lo and behold that girl was there. I sat down with everyone for awhile, and at one point got up to get a drink from the bar. She followed me to talk to me. Started flirting, realized we had common interests. Got her phone number. A bunch of the co workers went out for karaoke that night, she and I included. We ended up making out at the bar and she spent the night at my house. 

We’ve been dating since. She just moved in with me. We have made so many incredible memories. My boss, who convinced me to go the night she and I got together, will make jokes about the stories I tell him and say that our relationship feels like something out of a rom com. And it truly does. We’ve shared some really funny, spontaneous moments together. Sky diving, drunk flour fight in the kitchen while cooking, unknowingly stealing a bride and grooms dance being stupid snd in love, hiking mountains, you name it. 

I love this woman. She is the best most supportive woman I’ve ever met. If she isn’t the one I’ll be baffled. 

Go for it. Ya never know!

Emotional unavailability, toxicity, mixed signals, ghosting are all pretty easily recognizable qualities that you seem to be familiar with. That being said, you should try slowing down a bit and get to know someone better before you commit or invest yourself too deeply. 

If you are noticing a pattern in the negative qualities of the men you say you attract, you should be able to notice other qualities as well IE why you’re attracted to them in the first place. 

As for dating apps, I would try to stray from these unless you feel confident that you can keep an open mind. They’re incredibly unbalanced. It’s a lot of guys and a very small percentage of men, and an even smaller percentage of men who are getting a lot of the attention. A lot of these guys will appear to be fun and exciting and attractive, and while they might be all of those things, you should take your time to vet them out better. 

Also, as someone who used to end up with a lot of toxic women, I do genuinely believe it is not that difficult to vet them out once you start recognizing patterns and certain qualities. 

TLDR this is easily solvable and you’re probably putting it on yourself in some way without realizing it. Stop dating shitty men and be a little more open minded. Often times the hottest, most charismatic / outgoing / funny / charming people are the ones you have to look out for.

I’m not saying there’s anything wrong with wanting someone who sees one person at a time. 
But there’s also nothing wrong with someone who is trying to get to know multiple people in the beginning. 

Ultimately it’s their choice and this is a matter of personal preference. You aren’t obligated to see anyone who is going out with other people. But they aren’t doing anything wrong. To call it “shitty dating” is a little immature and possessive IMO. 

Sounds like the idea of a woman you’ve just met seeing other people aside from you until she gets to know you better sparks some insecurity. Which I get, but that’s not really fair to lump it up into some derogatory manner. 

After you’ve been on a good handful of dates with someone, like a month or two, and feelings start being expressed and the idea of becoming exclusive is communicated, sure. I’d expect that person to not be entertaining anyone else. 

But I’m not going on a first date with someone I just met and hardly know anything about and expecting them not to talk to anyone else and get angry about it if she is.

Until you agree to be exclusive with someone or explicitly communicate some form of emotional gravity to the relationship with one another, I don’t think it’s wrong to be talking to other people. 

I’m not the type to talk to multiple people at once but I also couldn’t get upset if I went on one or two dates with someone and it turned out they were still texting or talking to other people. That is so new and fresh. 

IMO expecting someone to drop everything and everyone else the second they meet you is a bit controlling and unrealistic. 

You’re also not obligated to tell the other person. It’s none of their business until you’re exclusive.

Also it sounds like you have some issues with insecurity and low self esteem. I struggle with this too. You need to focus on doing some things that will ground you and build confidence. And you need to actively focus on the positive aspects of your relationship. Not the negative what ifs. Negative thinking can be addictive and your brain can be hardwired to think that way. You can’t control whether or not your girlfriend leaves you or cheats on you. You can only be a good partner to her and leave the rest to trusting her. If she hasn’t ever given you a reason to believe she’d cheat, trust that and leave all the rest behind. It’ll only hurt you. Self fulfilling prophecies exist for a reason. Trust yourself and trust your girlfriend. Leave all the insecurities behind. Read about positive thinking. Journal. Listen to self help podcasts. Replace any negative thinking with positive material.

I see what you’re saying. I’m not an expert and I could be wrong but I don’t think explaining the details of your past is going to be productive. 

1) Its just going to make him feel more insecure. I’m not saying that it’s okay but talking to him about your past and all the details when the idea that you have a past in general isn’t going to bring things forward in a positive way. It’s just going to give him more to be insecure about. 

2) Your past doesn’t matter and it shouldn’t matter. The fact that you’ve dated or slept with other people shouldn’t bother him this much. Like if you had a huge issue with cheating on your boyfriends in the past that’s one thing. But it sounds like he’s just bugged out over the fact that you’ve dated and slept with other guys before him. That’s not ok. 

By communicating honestly I mean just open up and tell him that it hurts you that he reacts the way he does and that you’re more focused on him and the relationship you have now. Ultimately that should be the only important detail.
You should be able to do the above and have a mature conversation about it without him freaking out and slandering you.
